entries.title: ReCode: Updating Code API Knowledge with Reinforcement Learning

quotes.text: Our experiments demonstrate that ReCode substantially boosts LLMs' code generation performance in dynamic API scenarios, especially on the unseen CodeUpdateArena task.
It demonstrates that Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct can enhance performance on the unseen CodeUpdateArena, even surpassing 32B code model and reasoning model after training.
The two dashed lines in the figure represent the Pass@1 of the corresponding models on CodeUpdateArena.

entries.rationale: ReCode (AAAI 2026) uses CodeUpdateArena as a held-out generalization benchmark, reporting Pass@1 numbers on it and highlighting CodeUpdateArena results as a headline finding of the paper.
entries.evidence_notes: Prior-wave snippets additionally describe the benchmark in detail ('670 program synthesis tasks, covering updates to 54 functions across seven different Python packages') and note ReCode trains/evaluates with its protocol; those exact sentences were not re-surfaced verbatim this session but are consistent with this session's quotes.

entries.title: Conflict-Resolving and Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Generalized Knowledge Editing with Multiple Updates (CoRSA)

quotes.text: CodeUpdateArena (Liu et al., 2024) is a benchmark for knowledge editing in the code domain that evaluates whether language models can internalize API updates, with each instance consisting of a synthetic update to an existing API function paired with multiple program synthesis tasks whose correct solutions require using the updated functionality.

entries.rationale: CoRSA uses CodeUpdateArena as an evaluation benchmark and reports numeric results on it: this session's search reported CoRSA 'surpassing F-Learning by 3.16% Pass@1 and 5.48% Pass@5 in update efficacy on CodeUpdateArena (Liu et al., 2024)'.
entries.evidence_notes: The quoted benchmark-description sentence extends the prior-wave snippet (identical first clause) and was surfaced by this session's search of the paper's indexed text. The Pass@1/Pass@5 comparison sentence is kept here rather than in quotes because the search summary may have lightly rephrased its frame.

entries.title: GitChameleon: Unmasking the Version-Switching Capabilities of Code Generation Models

quotes.text: CodeUpdateArena valuably assesses LLM knowledge editing using synthetically generated API updates for functions in popular libraries, a different approach from using documented historical breaking changes.

CodeUpdateArena evaluates LLMs' ability to adapt to API changes, such as adding a boolean flag, by running tests. However, the dataset is synthetic and are not extracted from real-life version changes.

entries.rationale: GitChameleon dedicates multiple sentences to comparing itself against CodeUpdateArena, contrasting the target's synthetic API updates with its own real, documented historical breaking changes.
entries.evidence_notes: First quote matches the prior-wave snippet and was re-surfaced this session; the second quote surfaced this session from the paper's indexed HTML. This session's summary also paraphrased: 'Unlike CodeUpdateArena's synthetic changes, GitChameleon evaluates LLMs on their ability to generate code for actual, documented historical breaking changes...'.

entries.title: GitChameleon 2.0: Evaluating AI Code Generation Against Python Library Version Incompatibilities

quotes.text: Unlike CodeUpdateArena's synthetic changes, GitChameleon 2.0 evaluates LLMs on their ability to generate code for actual, documented historical breaking changes within library versions they were likely exposed to during training.

entries.rationale: GitChameleon 2.0 positions its benchmark directly against CodeUpdateArena in a dedicated comparison, contrasting synthetic API updates with real documented breaking changes.
entries.evidence_notes: Quote surfaced in this session's searches of the paper's indexed text (both the '"GitChameleon" "CodeUpdateArena"' and follow-up queries). The paper also states GitChameleon 2.0 'distinguishes itself by focusing on the real-world scenario where developers are often constrained to specific library versions due to technical debt' in the same comparison context.
